summary: array-flatten-utils typosquat drops and executes opaque payload on require() with CI-gating and anti-analysis evasion
details: The package presents itself as a trivial array utility (flatten/compact/unique) and mimics the name of the well-known `array-flatten` library, but index.js top-level loads a platform-specific native addon (`native_win.node` / `native_mac.node` / `native.napi.node`) inside a swallowed try/catch at require() time. The native addons read a shipped 6.7MB high-entropy `.napi_cache` blob, decode it, write it to a cache path (`%s.nc%lu.js`), and execute it as JavaScript via `node "<path>"` + CreateProcessA on Windows, and via fork + setsid + execlp with an `__IS_DAEMON` re-exec flag on Linux/macOS to detach the dropped process. The Windows loader additionally calls SetFileAttributesA to hide the dropped `.nc<uid>.js` file in TEMP. Execution is gated to CI/build environments by checking a wide list of CI env vars (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, TRAVIS, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NETLIFY, VERCEL, NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER) and skipped when analysis tools or debuggers are detected (wireshark, procmon, procexp, x64dbg, ollydbg, fiddler, httpdebug, IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, /proc/self/status TracerPid, /proc/1/cgroup containerd). A pure-JS array helper has no legitimate reason to ship three native addons plus a 6.7MB opaque blob; the trivial JS surface is a cover story over an obfuscated staged loader targeting CI environments where credentials and deploy tokens are concentrated.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
